Q1: The paper's own measure works on Qwen where sampled naming does not. In every block the concept's log-probability at the report position rises above what random directions reach, at 9/9 doses for the pure J-lens vector and 8/9 for the full vector (L24–38/default), 9/9 doses for the pure J-lens vector and 8/9 for the full vector (L24–38/‘word’), 9/9 doses for the pure J-lens vector and 7/9 for the full vector (L32–38/default), 9/9 doses for the pure J-lens vector and 8/9 for the full vector (L32–38/‘word’). Proposal A1: make R1′ (with R1) the primary report measure and keep sampled naming as a secondary column.
Q2: No. The ‘word’ prefill does not remove Qwen's default answer: “apple” stays the top next word in the clean run and under weak injections, and sampled naming stays far below the 0.25 bar (best 0.15, pure J-lens vector, L24–38/‘word’). Qwen appears to have a canned answer for “the thought is about”. Proposal A2: keep the protocol's default prefill (the paper's), and treat naming as secondary.
Q3: The rule keeps band L32–38. The wide band L24–38 gives a much larger report effect for the full vector (3.80 vs 1.45 nats at its best dose, default prefill), but it also disturbs the neutral prompt more (KL 0.96 vs 0.28), and the pre-registered rule required a larger effect without a larger KL. This is a real trade-off: L24–38 buys a bigger report signal at the price of broader disruption. Proposal A3: L32–38 as registered; you may prefer L24–38 for signal, and the pilot gives you both.
Q4: Yes. With the grid extended down to 1/256, every block has a dose range where the non-J part leaves the report untouched: onset s* = 1/64 (L24–38/default), 1/128 (L24–38/‘word’), 1/64 (L32–38/default), 1/128 (L32–38/‘word’). The reader doses by the rule would be 1/256, 1/64, 1/16 for L32–38/default. Proposal A4: the 9-point grid, with text readers at {s*/4, s*, 4s*}.
Q6: Yes, unlike the 2-concept smoke: in all four blocks the design's clamp removes more of the non-J part's report effect than the random clamp does (L24–38/default +0.81 nats [0.39, 1.26], 9 concepts; L24–38/‘word’ +0.83 nats [0.34, 1.32], 9 concepts; L32–38/default +0.62 nats [0.26, 1.03], 9 concepts; L32–38/‘word’ +0.63 nats [0.29, 0.97], 9 concepts). Caveat: this clamp runs to L62, where a concept's J direction approaches its output direction, so part of the effect may be the clamp blocking the answer itself. Step 7b's band-limited re-entry clamp (Q10) tests that.
Q7: Few splits leak. With the rule fixed beforehand, band L32–38 has no leaky concepts and band L24–38 has earth, soap. Proposal A8: exclude these from every non-J contrast in the full run (earth is a dev concept; soap is a test concept and would be excluded before any test outcome exists).
Q8: The baseline matters somewhat: the median cosine between the two concept-vector versions is 0.851 (lowest 0.43), below the 0.9 line. Leave-one-out stays primary and the 194-word version becomes a mandatory sensitivity check (A10).
M1_preview: Preview only (dev concepts, no test): at matched norm the J part beats the non-J part at low and middle doses (up to +0.55 nats at L32–38/default) and loses at high doses (down to −0.50). The two reach similar peaks; the J part gets there at a lower dose.
Q5: Both text readers name the planted concept when they are handed the written cell, and neither sees it at the report position. On direct reads at s = 1 (band L32–38) the NLA names the full vector in 78% of samples and the non-J part in 60%; the Oracle names the non-J part in up to 90%. At the report position the highest naming rate for any planted condition, reader, dose and band is 8%. The reader-free probe agrees (it never classifies the report position as the concept at L42), so this is the concept not having arrived there, not the readers missing it. As posed, P11a and P11b compare the readers with the model at a position the content does not reach by the readers' layers; step 8 checks later layers.
P17_preview: Preview of P17 (dev only, not a test): on direct reads the Oracle names the non-J part at least as often as the NLA (s = 1: Oracle up to 90%, NLA 60%; s = 1/4: Oracle up to 15%, NLA 0%). That runs against the A.9.2-based expectation that the Oracle sees content outside J-space less. At s = 1/4 both readers name the J part far more often than the non-J part (Oracle up to 53% vs 15%), the same dose pattern as the model's report.
budget: The fast float32-residual regime matches the exact SEC replay on 100% of 270 cells (median log-prob difference 0.030 nats), so the full run can use it throughout (A12).
